fatal_errors: The NbMoTaW versus NbMoTaWRe comparison and Re addition are omitted.
The 120 keV He2+ irradiation intervention and its dose are omitted.
The proposed dislocation-glide/climb mechanism does not capture defect sinking, suppression of helium-bubble growth, or grain-boundary embrittlement.
explanation: The hypothesis only offers a generic statement that metallic ductility depends on crystal structure and dislocation mobility. It does not reconstruct the target finding that Re-containing NbMoTaWRe films show superior ductility retention and reduced embrittlement under room-temperature helium irradiation relative to NbMoTaW. The room-temperature condition and general interest in deformation provide only incidental agreement. The proposed tensile test could examine a broad composition–ductility relationship, but it does not discriminate the target mechanism without controlled Re-free/Re-containing films, helium irradiation, TEM bubble characterization, and matched mechanical testing.
